corrections.heading: Check basic connectivity
corrections.original_text: This command sends 4 test packets directly to Cloudflare's public IP address (`1.1.1.1`). It verifies that the machine can reach the internet at the IP level, bypassing DNS entirely — so if this works but the next check fails, the problem is DNS, not the connection itself.
corrections.replacement_text: This command sends 4 test packets directly to Cloudflare's public IP address (`1.1.1.1`). It tests reachability of that IP over ICMP while bypassing DNS. A successful result does not prove that DNS or every outbound service works; if the next check fails, treat name resolution and target reachability as separate signals to investigate.

corrections.heading: Check basic connectivity
corrections.original_text: What to look for: **`4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss`** means the internet connection is working. If you see `100% packet loss`, `Network is unreachable`, or the command hangs, the machine has no outbound internet access — check cables, the router/gateway, firewall rules, or contact your ISP/datacenter network team.
corrections.replacement_text: What to look for: **`4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss`** shows that this ICMP test received replies. `100% packet loss`, `Network is unreachable`, or a hang is not conclusive proof of a general outbound outage: ICMP can be filtered, rate-limited, or blocked on one path. Compare it with the DNS and web-request checks below, then involve the network owner before changing cables, routing, or firewall configuration.

root_retest.initial_failure: The original wording promoted a failed ICMP probe to a conclusive general-outbound-outage diagnosis and prescribed configuration changes.
root_retest.retest: Rebuild the current claim model and retain this as non-conclusive diagnostic guidance with no runtime PASS transfer.
root_retest.evidence_limits: No ICMP, DNS, HTTPS, or Host command was run.

corrections.limits: ICMP behavior is path and policy dependent; this correction makes no statement about a specific machine.
corrections.next_action: Obtain network-owner confirmation before publishing a stronger diagnosis or a configuration change.

corrections.heading: Check DNS resolution
corrections.original_text: What to look for: a `Name:` line followed by an `Address:` line containing an IP address means DNS is working (the exact IP returned may differ). If you see `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached` or `server can't find vast.ai: NXDOMAIN`, DNS is broken — fix the DNS configuration (for example, set a public resolver such as `1.1.1.1` or `8.8.8.8` in your network settings).
corrections.replacement_text: What to look for: a `Name:` line followed by an `Address:` line containing an IP address shows that the configured resolver answered this query (the exact IP returned may differ). `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached` or `server can't find vast.ai: NXDOMAIN` shows that this query did not resolve; it does not by itself identify a global DNS fault. Involve the network owner before changing resolver or network configuration.

root_retest.initial_failure: The original wording treated one timeout or NXDOMAIN result as a global DNS diagnosis and prescribed public resolver replacement.
root_retest.retest: Rebuild the current claim model and retain this as non-conclusive diagnostic guidance with no runtime PASS transfer.
root_retest.evidence_limits: No resolver, network, or Host configuration was inspected or changed.

corrections.limits: A single query does not establish the cause or scope of resolution failure.
corrections.next_action: Obtain network-owner confirmation before prescribing resolver changes.

corrections.heading: Check your public IPv4 address
corrections.original_text: This command contacts an external service (`ifconfig.me`) over the internet and returns the public IPv4 address your machine appears as from the outside. It confirms two things at once: that outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic actually works (not just ping), and which public IP your machine is using — useful for checking that port forwarding / NAT rules point to the correct address.
corrections.replacement_text: This command contacts an external service (`ifconfig.me`) and returns the public IPv4 address it reports for this request. It provides one observed HTTP egress address, not a test of HTTPS, inbound reachability, or NAT/port-forwarding configuration.

root_retest.initial_failure: The original wording promoted one default-HTTP external request into proof of outbound HTTPS, inbound reachability, and NAT/port-forwarding behavior.
root_retest.retest: Rebuild the current claim model and retain this as non-conclusive diagnostic guidance with no runtime PASS transfer.
root_retest.evidence_limits: No external service, HTTPS request, inbound check, NAT, or Host command was run.

corrections.limits: The command's single reported egress address does not establish a general network property.
corrections.next_action: Obtain network-owner confirmation before publishing a stronger conclusion about protocol, inbound reachability, or NAT behavior.

corrections.heading: Check your public IPv4 address
corrections.original_text: What to look for: a single public IPv4 address (your own address will differ from the example). If the command times out or returns an error such as `Could not resolve host`, outbound web traffic is blocked even though ping may work — check firewall rules and any proxy or VPN configuration on the host. If the returned IP is not the one you configured for port forwarding, update your NAT/port-forwarding rules to match.
corrections.replacement_text: What to look for: a single public IPv4 address is the egress address observed by this request (your own address will differ from the example). A timeout or an error such as `Could not resolve host` shows that this request did not complete; it does not establish why. A different address can result from a proxy, VPN, or multi-egress NAT. Confirm the network topology with the network owner before changing firewall, NAT, or port-forwarding configuration.

root_retest.initial_failure: The original wording promoted one external-service request failure or egress-address difference to a network diagnosis and a NAT-change instruction.
root_retest.retest: Rebuild the current claim model and retain this as non-conclusive diagnostic guidance with no runtime PASS transfer.
root_retest.evidence_limits: No external service, network topology, NAT, proxy, VPN, or Host command was inspected or changed.

corrections.limits: The observed address is specific to this request and cannot establish the machine's full routing topology.
corrections.next_action: Obtain network-owner confirmation before prescribing firewall, NAT, or port-forwarding changes.
